rationale: History (all simulator estimates, not hardware; Metal ran exact source/config/TIR, CUDA binary not executed; no global-optimality claim): attempt-00 (32x64x32,s3) passed at 147.72, attempt-01 (32x64x64,s2) best at 147.67, attempt-02 (32x128x32,s3) regressed to 148.28, attempt-03 (32x128x64,s1) clearly regressed to 196.54. Best region is block_N=64 with shallow-moderate staging; wider block_N=128 and block_K=64,s1 hurt, so widen footprint weight to 1.5 to penalize large smem/register tiles and tall-skinny register pressure, and ease pipeline weight to 1.5 since s1 was bad but s2/s3 within block_N=64 is the promising band. Launches stay 0.25 (M=32 already caps grid). M=32 forces block_M=32 (64/128 do not divide M), so domain [32]; other domains nonempty and feasible under shared_bytes=max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages,4*block_M*block_N)<=32768 plus hard 32768 cap. Next hypothesis: exploit the unexplored block_N=64 block_K=64 num_stages=3 region (2*64*96*3=36864 exceeds cap for s3, so cap will exclude; instead test block_N=128 block_K=32 s2: 2*32*160*2=20480 fits, versus block_N=64 block_K=32 s3) to see whether footprint weight selects a lower-smem tuple that beats 147.67; if it does not, next round narrow block_N to [64] and keep block_K=[32,64], num_stages=[2,3].
